newsitem.title: UK: Shell and BP slip on weak oil prices.
newsitem.headline: Shell and BP slip on weak oil prices.

text.p: Shares in oil companies British Petroleum Co Plc and Shell Transport and Trading Group Plc slipped on Friday on continuing depressed crude oil prices, analysts said.
"Further weaknesses in the oil price mean the sector as a whole is a bit weaker," Shawn Reynolds, analyst at Lehman Brothers said.
BP shares lost 7p to trade at 676-1/2p by 1115 GMT, while Shell stock dipped 5p to 10.36-1/2 stg.
"They're (Shell and BP) not dropping as fast as Enterprise (Oil Plc ) was yesterday, but now they're just catching up with the rest of the oil companies," Reynolds said.
Oil traders said world crude prices continued to sink as rising supplies outweighed slack spring demand, pushing oil into a lower price range not seen for nine months.

London front-month futures for bellwether North Sea Brent blend crude oil recovered slightly on Friday to trade at $18.29 a barrel, up 11 cents after closing 32 cents lower at $18.19 on Thursday in London.
Brent has plunged around 25 percent in the past three months.
